transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-27
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Liam Ortega (Redwood CSM), Marta Ruiz (Nautilus Head of AI), Devon Hayes (Platform Eng), Amir Khan (SRE), Riley Park (Product)

Summary:
Quick postmortem of the April 22 latency/cost spike that impacted Nautilus' checkout recommendation service, alignment on short-term mitigations (burst capacity, fallback model), and roadmap items to avoid recurrence (KV cache tuning, Dedicated sizing, auto-scaling policies, observability improvements).

Topics discussed: incident timeline, root causes, immediate mitigations, capacity sizing, cost tradeoffs, security/compliance notes, next steps for pilot and benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Okay everyone, thanks for joining. Uh this is Jordan from Redwood, I'll hand it to Marta for quick context but the plan is a 45-60 minute sync: postmortem + next steps, all that.
[00:10] Marta Ruiz: Yeah thanks, um the short version — on April 22 between 11:23 and 11:52 our checkout recommender started spiking p99 latency to like 2.4 seconds from our normal 700 ms, and cost per session jumped 3x. We routed to a smaller model as a fallback but UX hit was pretty bad.
[00:28] Speaker 1 (Amir?): We had a coupling in our batching config too, so requests were accumulating in the frontend batcher then timing out, so more retries.
[00:36] Priya Kapoor: Right, we looked at the traces you shared, and there were three things that lined up: an unexpected traffic burst from a marketing campaign, a cache miss storm on the prefix/KV cache, and an autoscale threshold that didn't trigger fast enough because of the minimum cooldown.
[00:52] Devon Hayes: Quick clarification — when you say KV cache miss storm, are you referring to the GPU KV cache eviction or the prefix cache in the app layer? Our telemetry shows both increased.
[01:02] Priya Kapoor: Mostly the runtime-level KV cache — the KV cache on the model side wasn't warm for the pattern of queries introduced, so more tokens were recomputed. Also we saw continuous batching accumulate bigger batches than expected which spiked tail latency.
[01:18] Marta Ruiz: We also have some network egress throttles in our cloud account that we suspected might have delayed cold-started warm-ups for new pods.
[01:25] Jordan Kim: That's a helpful detail — Amir, Devon, can you confirm if there was any change to egress rules around April 21–22?
[01:33] Amir Khan: No infra changes, but we did spin up more frontend pods for the campaign which increased connection churn. Might've exceeded some NAT gateway NAT translations, causing retries.
[01:44] Riley Park: And just to call out product impact — the ML team is seeing lower conversion during the window which maps to a revenue hit; we want to avoid surprises like this.
[01:53] Priya Kapoor: From Redwood's side we saw model instance CPU stayed low but GPU memory and KV cache misses climbed; that points to a model working set problem. We recommended a combination of: 1) pre-warming KV cache for the top X prefixes, 2) reducing continuous batching window for checkout route during promo windows, and 3) temporary Dedicated burst capacity to handle the initial ramp.
[02:14] Jordan Kim: We'll put this in the postmortem doc with concrete numbers, but to set expectations: Dedicated sizing will lower p99 but cost might increase slightly unless we couple it with quantization/packing and cache improvements.
[02:29] Marta Ruiz: Quantization is a bigger lift for us if it impacts accuracy; we have a strict threshold on recommendation quality. Are you seeing quality regressions with 8-bit quant?
[02:37] Priya Kapoor: On curated recommend workloads we saw negligible change for most open models when we used per-channel quant and a small calibration set, but you should run your eval set. We'll help with that. There's always a model-dependent risk.
[02:50] Devon Hayes: Can you remind us, Jordan, what the SLA behavior is if we move to Dedicated vs hosted?
[02:56] Jordan Kim: Sure. Hosted has best-effort availability with credits; Dedicated has reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, and an SLA for uptime and a p95 latency target at the pool level. For incidents like this Dedicated lets you isolate traffic to a customer pool so noisy neighbors are not a factor.
[03:15] Speaker 2 (Marta?): Is there an on-prem migration path if we need to maintain strict data residency for logs?
[03:22] Jordan Kim: Yep, Private deployment options include VPC and on-prem packages, with a private control plane. We'll share the architecture diagram. Also we have KMS/HSM integrations for keys.
[03:31] Amir Khan: We need to see audit logs and access history for the timeframe — SSO and SAML events around the incident.
[03:37] Liam Ortega: I'll attach the security pack — SOC2, encryption at rest/in transit, audit log samples. Jordan will share the specific timeline logs you asked for.
[03:47] Marta Ruiz: Thanks. Operationally, what's the fastest mitigation we can put in place before we change Dedicated sizing?
[03:53] Priya Kapoor: Short term: set a tighter continuous-batch max window for checkout route, enable aggressive prefix caching for the top 1k prefixes, and add a temporary routing policy to send heavy traffic to the fallback model earlier to limit tail latency. We can push those config changes in a few hours if you approve.
[04:10] Devon Hayes: If we route to fallback earlier, will we lose personalization? That's our concern.
[04:15] Priya Kapoor: The fallback is a smaller variant with slightly lower context length; personalization may be reduced, but you get sub-second p99 in our tests. It's a product trade: lower latency vs small quality delta.
[04:28] Marta Ruiz: Okay let's sketch acceptable thresholds — p99 below 1.2s, conversion drop <2% during fallback windows.
[04:36] Jordan Kim: Noted. We'll include the proposed thresholds in the postmortem and the runbook.
[04:43] Riley Park: On runway, we need clear cost numbers. When you say cost per session jumped 3x, can you break that down into model token costs vs infrastructure (GPU hours) and retries?
[04:53] Priya Kapoor: From our preliminary numbers: model token cost accounted for ~45% of the increase, instance time (because of longer wall-time per request) ~35%, and retries and extra orchestration ~20%. We'll provide a detailed CSV.
[05:06] Marta Ruiz: And how much would Dedicated reduce that delta?
[05:09] Jordan Kim: Depends on sizing and autoscale aggressiveness. If we recommend a Dedicated pool sized to your 99th percentile sustained during campaign peaks, you avoid the cold-start overhead and get better packing. Rough estimate: 25–40% reduction in per-session infrastructure cost assuming we also do cache warming.
[05:25] Amir Khan: Network constraints — if we do Dedicated in our VPC peering scenario, will we still hit the NAT gateway egress limits?
[05:32] Priya Kapoor: If it's within your VPC with Private deployment and direct peering, NAT egress is under your control; for hosted/dedicated we'll highlight recommended network allowances and keep the control plane light.
[05:45] Devon Hayes: On observability — we want more granular token-level tracing attached to request IDs; current traces aggregate too coarsely. Is that on the roadmap?
[05:54] Liam Ortega: Observability improvements are in Redwood Console roadmap — token-level cost breakdown and per-route tracing are scheduled. We might be able to expedite the checkout route tracing as a priority for Nautilus.
[06:05] Marta Ruiz: Can you do an ETA? We need token-level traces within the next sprint to validate fixes.
[06:10] Liam Ortega: I'll flag it with Product; aim is to get an engineering ETA by next week.
[06:15] Jordan Kim: Quick note on benchmarks — Priya, can you run a replay with their April 22 traffic and include two configs: hosted default, hosted with prefix-warm, and Dedicated recommended size?
[06:25] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we'll run three replays, capture p50/p95/p99 and token cost per session. We'll also try a quantized run if Nautilus wants to evaluate accuracy tradeoffs.
[06:35] Devon Hayes: We'll share anonymized traces after this call. Any other security blockers?
[06:40] Amir Khan: Ensure logs we share are scrubbed; we cannot include PII. We'll coordinate with your team.
[06:46] Jordan Kim: Understood.
[06:50] Riley Park: One more product ask: can we schedule a canary window for the new routing policy and have automatic rollback after X minutes if p99 spikes?
[06:58] Priya Kapoor: Yes, Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. We'll propose a canary config in the postmortem.
[07:07] Marta Ruiz: Sounds good. Let's talk about long-term: we are evaluating whether to contract Dedicated for the holiday peak season and maybe move checkout to Private if residency constraints increase. What's the typical lead time?
[07:20] Jordan Kim: For Dedicated there is capacity booking and we recommend 4–6 weeks lead time for large pools in a region. Private on-prem has a longer lead time depending on your procurement and network readiness — often 8–12 weeks.
[07:33] Devon Hayes: Procurement question — will Dedicated require a new contract or can we convert usage credits?
[07:38] Jordan Kim: Dedicated is a reserved capacity contract; we can discuss partial conversion depending on your current commitment. Liam from CSM will help.
[07:45] Liam Ortega: I'll follow up with procurement templates after this meeting.
[07:48] Marta Ruiz: Okay, recap please?
[07:50] Jordan Kim: Quick recap: Jordan to share postmortem and logs by 4/29; Priya to run three replay benchmarks and return p95/p99 and cost breakdown by 5/4; Nautilus to send anonymized traces by 4/30; we recommend immediate short-term mitigations (batch window, prefix warming, earlier fallback) that Priya can apply with approval — if accepted we can push changes in hours; longer term Dedicated sizing proposal and quant evals in two weeks; security docs from Liam by 4/30.
[08:22] Marta Ruiz: That covers it. Thanks everyone.
[08:26] Jordan Kim: Thanks — we'll follow up with the doc and a 2-week check-in invite.

End of transcript.

- Preliminary incident dashboard (Grafana link) — will be in postmortem doc

Explicit next meeting: Health check / benchmark review scheduled tentatively for 2026-05-11 (Liam to confirm).
